title: Detroit grocery drive-time, walking, and radius demographics benchmark

routing.note: Source server updates. Captured output shapes and request settings are preserved in each catchment.

methods_and_limits: Matched each public store address to a Census address-range point. The route engine snapped that point to a network edge. A snapped position does not establish a storefront entrance.
Computed a three-mile radius in EPSG:26917 and inbound 10-minute walk and drive polygons with Valhalla. No time-specific traffic input, observed visits, or door-to-door timing was used.

Joined the 2024 Census block groups to 2020 block internal points. Weighted people and employed residents by the 2020 population share in each catchment and household counts by the 2020 housing-unit share. Where a group had no base for a weight, used its intersected area share. The weight assumes that smaller-area settlement patterns are relevant to the 2020–2024 survey period.
Separately reran each count using full-polygon area shares to show allocation sensitivity. Block internal-point fractions can move in jumps across a boundary.

Applied the same weights to the release estimates and each of the 80 signed variance replicates. Calculated the margin at 90 percent confidence using the square root of 4/80 times the sum of squared replicate deviations, multiplied by 1.645. Calculated percentages and differences inside each matched replicate before applying the same formula.

The margin measures ACS sampling uncertainty for the chosen geometry and allocation weights. It omits network, time-dependent travel, entrance, sampling-frame, and spatial allocation errors. These estimates describe residents and households associated with the modeled catchments, rather than customer counts, store performance or measured foot traffic.
